summary: Multiplexed HTTP/2 streaming sessions freeze after large system prompt and client-side buffer backpressure
description:
Issue summary: Multiple ComposeAI customers on Dedicated capacity report that streaming chat connections established over HTTP/2 (multiplexed) appear to 'freeze' after an initial burst of tokens. The connection remains open but no new data is received until the client hits its local idle timeout and closes the stream.

Impact: Several long-running chat sessions (context size > 32k tokens, large system prompt + file attachments) are affected. Users observe frozen streams for 20-120 seconds before client-side reconnects. This results in poor UX and lost partial responses for long-form generation. The problem is reproducible in eu-west production with the customer's dedicated pool.

Observed behavior: Connection established, first ~100–300 tokens stream normally, then a silence window with TCP connection still established. Server-side metrics show the worker is still processing (CPU/GPU utilization on worker unchanged or slightly increased), but no data is flushed to the client. Edge proxy shows repeated HTTP/2 WINDOW_UPDATE behavior and occasional RST_STREAM from client after idle.

Expected behavior: Streaming responses should continue to flush tokens to the client progressively; no persistent silence unless model actually pauses generation or a clean error is raised.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer sends chat request via HTTP/2 with multiplexing enabled and a large system prompt (~25k chars) plus attachments.
2) Request routed to dedicated pool in eu-west and model redwood-13b-preview is used.
3) Observe streaming start (SSE/WebSocket over H2) and token flow for first few hundred tokens.
4) After a burst, tokens stop arriving while worker continues compute until completion or until client-level idle timeout triggers.
5) Client receives no error; eventually closes and retries, sometimes receiving truncated output.

investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: HTTP/2 flow-control window exhaustion at the edge leading to backpressure where the edge queues DATA frames but does not forward them to the downstream connection to the client (client-side buffer full).

What we checked:
- Worker logs: model kept generating; no OOMs or worker restarts.
- Network: no network partition; TCP connections remain ESTABLISHED.
- Edge proxy: high number of WINDOW_UPDATE frames and queued DATA frames observed.
- Client: ComposeAI's client reported they use HTTP/2 multiplexing and very small client-side read window, and do not issue timely WINDOW_UPDATEs for large initial payloads.
- Autoscaling/evictions: A few worker replacements correlated with the window stalling but were not root cause.

Root cause (working theory): combination of (1) client-side small receive window/read throttling (ComposeAI client), (2) edge-proxy H2 implementation delaying forwarding when per-connection flow-control thresholds are hit, and (3) long initial system prompts increasing time-to-first-flush so the edge's heuristics for flushing are suboptimal. These together create a silent period while the worker waits for the edge/client to accept more bytes.

Risk assessment: Affects customers using HTTP/2 multiplexing with long contexts across dedicated pools. Not all dedicated customers affected; correlated with specific client implementations that throttle reads aggressively.

2026-03-10 15:28 - SRE (Marcus Li): Reproduced internally against a dedicated pool using the customer's client binary. Observed identical WINDOW_UPDATE pattern and queued DATA in edge-proxy. Adding trace IDs to linked issue.

2026-03-11 09:41 - ComposeAI (Customer): Confirmed they ship a custom HTTP/2 client that sets low receive buffer sizes to reduce memory usage on mobile. They're willing to test changes to client WINDOW_UPDATE timing if needed.

2026-03-12 11:16 - Edge team (Lena Park): Deployed a canary change to edge-proxy that increases the hysteresis on forwarding queued DATA for H2 connections. Small improvement in our lab repro; will monitor prod. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/542

2026-03-13 22:05 - Support (Anita Gomez): Applied temporary workaround for ComposeAI's dedicated pool: enabled aggressive partial-flush (flush-on-chunk) and bumped H2 connection-level window. Observed reduced incidence (from ~15% -> ~2%). Customer confirmed improvement in staging.

2026-03-14 08:33 - SRE (Marcus Li): Plan to backport edge-proxy fix to all dedicated eu-west edge nodes overnight; schedule a post-deploy monitoring run for 24h. Creating follow-up engineering task to harden server-side flush heuristics and add telemetry on queued-data per-connection.
resolution: Workaround implemented: enabled partial flush and increased H2 connection window size for affected dedicated pool; applied edge-proxy canary change. Full fix targeted in PRs linked above to instrument queued-data thresholds and improve flush heuristics. Customer asked for post-deploy verification before closing.
next_steps: 1) Roll edge-proxy change to all eu-west dedicated nodes (Marcus Li). 2) Add server-side telemetry for queued DATA frames and per-stream paused duration (engineering). 3) Coordinate with ComposeAI to test client WINDOW_UPDATE cadence changes in their next release. 4) Re-evaluate after 24h of rollout; if stable, close ticket and document in streaming runbook.
